text: Dragon tortoises were terrestrial creatures that, like their aquatic cousins the dragon turtles, were related to dragons.
The Dragon of the Deeps was an enormous dragon turtle that lived within the depths of the Deepwash as of the late 14 century DR.

The cook, simply known as the Dragonborn Grillmaster, was an adventuring Sunite pitmaster famed for manning the Grillin' Grounds during the annual Midsummer Festival of Sune in Neverwinter in the late 15 century DR.

Drow (; ), also known as dark elves, deep elves, night elves, under-elves, and the Dark Ones among orcs, were a dark-skinned sub-race of elves that predominantly lived in the Underdark. They were hated and feared due to their cruelty, though some non-evil and an even smaller number of good drow existed.

Duergar (; ), also known variously as dark dwarves, gray dwarves, underdwarves, or uhubreen, were a subterranean subrace of dwarves. They carved out an existence in the Underdark, often near volcanoes. Their kinship to other dwarven subraces could be compared to that of the drow to surface elves.

Drogan Droganson was a renowned dwarf wizard, cleric of Mystra, and secret member of the Harpers who opened a school for adventurers in Hilltop in the Silver Marches, after retiring from his own adventuring life.
Dryads (), also known as wood nymphs, were fey-maidens who acted as the protectors of forests and trees.

Dugmaren Brightmantle () was a lesser dwarven deity of learning and innovation, and patron of dwarven scholars and free thinkers. The domain of the Wandering Tinker was the gathering of knowledge regardless of its utility and the creation of novel inventions using the various findings. The Errant Explorer embodied the progressive side of the conservative Stout Folk, and the exploratory spirit that led to acts of creativity.

Draguth Endroun is the elderly and reclusive leader of the druidic circle known as the Knightswood Nine. A stubborn and short-tempered man, Draguth is often found fighting with the other members of the group. He retains his leadership over the others by acting more powerful than he is along with possessing a brilliant store of knowledge about the King's Forest.
Druxus Rhym was the Zulkir of Transmutation within the Red Wizards of Thay in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

King Drasna Bluemantle, also known as Drasna the Fortunate was a human paladin of Torm and the ruler of the kingdom of Ulgarth in southeast Faerûn in the mid-to-late 14th century DR. He ruled from the city of Orvyltar.
Drasek Riven was a one-eyed, former Zhentarim assassin and longtime rival of Erevis Cale.
Drisinil Melarn was the matron mother of House Melarn until her death and its fall in the year 1372 DR.

King Duar "Longyears" Obarskyr was the 52 monarch in the Obarskyr dynasty and ruler of Cormyr from the , to the . He was one of the most renowned warrior-kings in Cormyr's history, second only to King Dhalmass. During Duar's reign, the kingdom grew in size and strength. The army was larger, better trained, and better equipped, and the lands of Irongates, Jarthroon, and Wheloon were annexed.
Dugald was a human man of Damara and a cleric of Ilmater and St. Dionysus. He was a famous adventuring cleric of the Bloodstone Lands and one of its saviors.
Droze was a fisherman and later the innkeeper of The Mermaid's Purse in Corth, Aglarond, in the mid-14 century DR.
Dragonwrought kobolds were rare members of the kobold race with a stronger connection to their draconic ancestors.
Drakar was a human man. He served as a cook to both the Red Brigade mercenaries and later the Vipers bandits.
Marquise Dresimil Chûmavh was the matriarch of House Chûmavh, a drow clan that occupied Tower Chûmavhraele in a huge cavern beneath Ravens Bluff in the late 15 century DR.
Drisinil Barrison Del'Armgo was a novice priestess of Lolth at Arach-Tinilith in Menzoberranzan and a member of House Barrison Del'Armgo in the late 14 century DR.
Drann Barrow was a member of the Zhentarim who lived in Neverwinter in 1484 DR.

Dralmorrer Borngray was an elf who served as caretaker of Castle Naerytar for the Black Dragon Wyrmspeaker Rezmir of the reformed Cult of the Dragon under Severin Silrajin. He was also member of the Eldreth Veluuthra.
Duagloth Seerear was a drow of House Dhuurniv involved in the Zhent invasion of Shadowdale in the Year of Risen Elfkin, 1375 DR.

Dualah was a female human cleric of Umberlee in Hillsfar in 1367 DR. She tended to the shrine of Umberlee there. Lord Maalthiir seemed interested in her — according to a rumour, they were romantically involved. However, Dualah was a follower of Mordak Brelliar, Maalthiir's apprentice, who tried to use this to his advantage, to gain information on Maalthiir. Dualah knew nothing about these plots.

Dretches were the least powerful of tanar'ri demonkind, petty, ugly wretches that were casually sacrificed by higher-ranking demonic entities. Doomed to a likely eternity of disappointment, they did little but wallow in stinking mobs and their own self-pity while bemoaning their fate.
Drullister was a phaerimm and the leader of a small hive in Synod in 1375 DR.

Dreylil Andrus was captain of the palace guard of King Yarin Frostmantle of the Damara circa 1484 DR. Following the assassination of King Frostmantle, he worked with Court Wizard Red Mazzie to deflect suspicion from Queen Concettina Delcasio in order to ensure a peaceful transition to her rule.
Drayson Fivestars () was a member of the Brotherhood of the Cloak in Mulmaster in 1491 DR.
Drake "Deepcups" was a sage in Iriaebor in 1358 DR. His area of expertise was dwarf history. He charged twice the normal fee for consultation, but had a soft spot for a good ale.

Du-yang was a prince of the kingdom of Silla in the land of Choson (later known as Koryo) before the mid–14th century DR. Under the influence of a love potion from the Quang Muku Forest, Prince Du-yang of Silla fell in love with a plotting woman and was slain by her jealous husband.

Drakosa, also known by the full name Drakosa yn Sallah yi Manshaka, was a petty Calishite noble who traveled to Maztica in the 14 century DR, becoming the sole Calishite landholder of the New Amnian colonies during that time.
Dral Thelev was an one-eyed half-orc innkeeper in Everlund sometime after the War of the Silver Marches.
Captain Drashk was a sea-captain in Waterdeep sometime after the War of the Silver Marches.
Dramar Lornen was a collector from the "Royal Keep" of Ironhar in Eskorn, Laerakond.
Droop was a goblin and slave to the Redbrand bugbears who dwelt in Tresendar Manor circa 1491 DR.
Dreb was a barbed devil in Avernus, first layer of the Nine Hells, in the late 15 century DR.
Dror Ragzlin was a hobgoblin True Soul of the Cult of the Absolute.
Captain Dratharion was the leader of the mercenary company of the Griffons, secretly a Zhentarim agent, who worked for Matagar Bugo in Daggerford in 1372 DR.
Dreppin was a monk of the Avowed who dwelled within the fortress-library of Candlekeep during the mid–14 century DR.
Drawmij was a great mage from Oerth who was known to have visited Toril. He was known by a few inhabitants of the Realms, and his spells were used throughout.
Du'Quelve Hunzrin was a priestess of House Hunzrin in Menzoberranzan in the early 14 century DR.
Dread linnorms were the largest species of linnorm, and were easily distinguishable by their two heads.

Drogthu Elfeater was an orc warband leader of the kingdom of Many-Arrows in the late 15 century DR. He served under commander Vansi Bloodscar in their occupation of the River District of Neverwinter in the late 1470s DR.
Drethna was a half-orc worshiper of Talos and a member of the anchorites of Talos active in southern Neverwinter Wood in the late 15 century DR.
High Priestess Duatha Lindar was the ranking priestess of the Lady's Hall, a temple dedicated to Tymora, in Ordulin in the .
Drigor Bersk was a cleric of Ilmater who fought by King Gareth Dragonsbane's side in . He was instrumental to ending the Rage of Dragons.
Drizhal was a young soldier and lieutenant in the allied army of the Dalelands that lived and died during the mid–14 century DR.

Dren was one of the Blades of the Old Man in the fortress of Sentinelspire. He was a part of the team accompanying Sauk to look for Kheil and secure the Erael'len in the Northern Shalhoond in Tarsakh of , conspiring to kill the Old Man of the Mountain. Kerlis, Valmir and Dren stayed behind to watch Berun and Lewan when Sauk decided to hunt down some yaqubi, expecting them to be carrying gold. Berun disabled them and fled, though Sauk's party caught up to them by the next morning.
Druk was a goblin warrior and devotee of the Absolute that dwelled within the Shattered Sanctum during the late 15 century DR.
Dregaul Matrell was one of the three siblings, the second generation of House Matrell, a noble mercantile family of Arrabar and the family's head as of 1362 DR.
Dressus was a corrupt Captain of the Municipal Guard of Arrabar in the Vilhon Reach circa 1373 DR.
Dramvar was an eladrin noble and the Master of the Spire of Summer's Mist on the Watch on Forever's Edge, together with Eloar.
Dukar Krabbellor, who was nicknamed Hammerhand, was a laborer inhabiting the city of Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Duilya Evendusk was an inhabitant of Cormanthor in the 3 century DR.
Drannor was an elf from Cormanthor known to be the first to marry a dwarf.
Drik was a thug and robber who operated near Yhaunn in Sembia in 1373 DR.
Drueena was the green hag who dwelt on a "haunted" island in Northwest Faerûn in the late 15 century DR.
Drakkar Von Damm was an adventuring paladin from the city of Ravens Bluff, active in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Dryfle Doon was a gold dwarf commoner, displaced by The Absolute, and as a refugee, sought shelter in Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Drussuvissill was a hin farmer, displaced by The Absolute, and as a refugee, sought shelter in Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Driander was a Netherese arcanist who taught at the Institute for Sorcerous Imagery in Eileanar until its destruction in .
Dravidge was a clerk who worked at Candulhallow's Funeral Arrangements in the Heapside district of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Droona Shveitz was an inhabitant of Baldur's Gate and the wife of Agnes Shveitz in the late 15 century DR.
Draskos Crownsilver was a nobleman of Cormyr and a head of the Crownsilver family in the late 15 century DR.
Dralkin was a swordcaptain with the Watch of Suzail, Cormyr, in the late 15 century DR.
Drongo Bixworth, husband of Florean Bixworth, was an inhabitant of the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in late 15 century DR.
Dugg was a Cashguard Basher in the employ of the Counting House of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Drijm Stoneaxe was a dwarven advisor to Dagult Neverember in Neverwinter during the late 15 century DR.
Dreena Covely was a Sharran infiltrator from the hidden Cloister of Sombre Embrace in the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Droo Falbo was a member of the Gondian clergy and a foundry worker from the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Duethaea Lauraunfeir () was a Chosen of Mystra of the Delimbiyr Vale in the 9 century DR.
Drarra was an inhabitant of the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Duddy Dudderken was an inhabitant of the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
The Duchess of Wyndrake was a noblewoman living near Neverwinter in the late years of the 15 century DR.
Drykal was a blacksmith from Luskan during the late 15 century DR.

Dravo Flymm was a merchant and cobbler who, alongside his wife, Sally Flymm, ran Flymm's Cobblers in the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR. Sally was also the mother of the infamous Lord Gortash, one of the leaders of the Cult of the Absolute.
Drybeldiyx was a dragonborn inhabitant of the Lower City on Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Drake Elderwood was a human ranger who roamed the wilds of Faerûn in the mid 14 century DR.
Dreak was a half-orc who was former slave turned pirate and the first mate of the infamous Scimitar of Fire, which was active on the Sea of Swords in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Dram Kallen is an alchemist and inventor of the Silver Stake gas bomb, a device used by the Silver Stake to subdue and capture lycanthropes. He is also a founding member of the Silver Stake organization itself. He was born in Baldur's Gate and has lived there his entire life.

Duggan McKnuckles was a dwarf with a yellow beard. He was the brother of Tred McKnuckles. He was killed in 1370 DR when a band of orcs and frost giants attacked the caravan in which he was travelling.
Durman Hilesta is the carpenter and bouncer of The Old Skull Inn in Shadowdale.
Dura Gerathu was a male ranger who lived in the Brynwood forest in the Vast in the mid–14 century DR.
Dunlath Darlspur was an inhabitant of the city of Wheloon in Cormyr. Dunlath operated a smithy there around 1358 DR.
Dulwar the Leatherworker was a male human who ran his own leatherwork business in Dagger Falls. He was a friend to and spy for Randal Morn.
Sultan Duncan el Ashnarti was the ruler of the city of Keltar in Calimshan as late as 1370 DR.

Dunn Tenwealth was a priest of Torm in the mid–14 century DR. He served as high priest at the Temple of Torm's Coming in Tantras before and during the Time of Troubles and was a member of the city's High Council.
Duromil the Fearless () was a rogue in Waterdeep in 1372 DR.
Captain Dunmish was an envoy from Icewind Dale who went to Neverwinter to recruit adventurers to fight Akar Kessel and the black ice menace.
Dunstanny was a halfling personal assistant to the wizard Parwyyd Hanifar in the mid–14 century DR.
Durkotl was the scarred leader of the Tezat settlement in Nexal in 1362 DR.
Durana Shaleel was a member of the Council of Seven Burghers in 1368 DR.

Dread Wavelord Dumai Arachneie was a Tashalan human cleric and waveservant of Umberlee in Lapaliiya in the mid–14 century DR. Circa 1373 DR, he was the ruler of Ilyaport, a Lapaliiyan town dedicated to Umberlee.
Durnan the Sixth was the innkeeper of the Yawning Portal in Waterdeep in the 1470s DR. He was a direct descendant of Durnan, the inn's original founder.
Dundast Hulrel was the Lord of Corm Orp in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Dur-baagal was one of the primordials who fought against the gods before the Sundering of Abeir-Toril.

Dunsel was a dwarf with a dream during the early years of Khôltar, the Iron City. In the Year of the Molten Anvils, 366 DR, he finally got the funds from his Shieldlord and friend, Amberu Khôltar, to build a road paved in stone from Eartheart to Khôltar. It took years, and skeptical residents of the Iron City referred to the project as "Dunsel's Dream", but when it was finally completed, dozens of new heavy wagons (invented in the Year of the Bitter Smile, 368 DR, by Ulbrask Hael) took advantage of the Dunsel Trail and brought a surge of prosperity to the town as it became a busy trade center. Dunsel didn't stop there: in the years to follow, he continued on, extending his road hundreds of m
Dundeld Nanther was the Lord Envoy of the Council of Lords in Melvaunt around 1367 DR. His death in 1373 nearly started a new civil war inside the city.
First Guardian Dumal Erard was a paladin-priest of Helm, and an adventuring member of the Company of Crazed Venturers who later went on to found the community of Helm's Hold during the 14 century DR.
Durakh Haan was a devout cleric of Luthic who dwelled within the ruins of Citadel Rashemar during the late 14 century DR.
Dunatis was a minor interloper deity of mountains and peaks who originated from another plane of existence.
Durlan was a moon elven wizard inhabiting Selgaunt in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Durgar the Just was the head of the city watch in Westgate in the .
Dundar was a blacksmith and inhabitant of Tilverton in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Duroamyn "Deathstrike" Steelhawk was a famous adventurer and archer in northwest Faerûn in the 14 century DR.
Lord Dureth was a member of the Swords of Evereska that bravely defended his home city during a crisis that broke out in the late 14 century DR.
High Radiance Durneth Seafarer was the leader of the temple known the Tower of the Morning.
Duneden was an old apothecary inhabiting the city of Daggerford in the Western Heartlands in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Duracles () was the pit fiend of the Nine Hells that oversaw the domain of Mirror Maelstrom on the plane of Avernus.
Captain Durham Shaw was a leader among the Neverwinter Guard in the late 15 century DR.
Dunbold Laraeikan was a retired warrior inhabiting Waterdeep, City of Splendors, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Dundold Buldharroaz was a baker inhabiting Waterdeep, the City of Splendors, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Tracker Dullwill was a cultist of the Absolute who served his goddess during the late 15 century DR.
Dumic, who was nicknamed the Red, was a rancher inhabiting the town of Ashabenford in Mistledale during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Durang Head-taker was an orc chieftain inhabiting Tarkhaldale, the Lost Dale, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Durm Goroy was a convicted criminal from the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Durexter Dagohnlar was a merchant from Marsember in the late 14 century DR.
Durbem was a dwarf artisan of the Goblinbreaker Clan who resided in Baldur's Gate in the late 14 century DR.
Dune hags were monstrous humanoids related to the annis hag, who inhabited deserts and wastelands.
Duna Duckfens was a duergar from the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Durlim was one of the bandits under the Iron Fox in the mid–8 century DR.
Durnhal was King of Corwell in the Moonshae Isles during the mid-to-late 3 century DR.
Dumathoin Thunderstone was a Captain of the Guard of Thunderholme, some time before the fall of the city in the . The dwarf's bracers eventually found their way to Aurgloroasa's treasure hoard.
Dumpy Dumpling was once the headliner performing for the Circus of the Last Days sometime in or before the late 15 century DR.
Lord Mage Dunsteen was a wizard of Mlembryn in the early-to-mid 3 century DR.

Grand Knight Dunstan Cormaeril was the commander of the Purple Dragon Knights order of amethyst dragon–riding knights and a member of the Cormaeril noble family of Cormyr at the turn of the 16 century DR.
Elmandar was an elf or half-elf mage and noted astronomer in the city of Bral on the Rock of Bral in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. He was the proprietor of Elmandar's Star Charts.
Elissa Tarixon was the mysterious Queen who ruled the amazon isle of Ixinos off the coast of the Vilhon Reach in the late 14 century DR.
Elvarado Chaserperi was one of the potential heirs to the Chaserperi clan in the late mid-14 century DR.
Elthure Vildenof was a former aspiring Red Wizard and later member of the Stalwart Lions as of .
Elestar was a musician and street performer inhabiting Waterdeep, the City of Splendors, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Elgorel was a bartender inhabiting Waterdeep, City of Splendors, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Elyme was one of the three dryads enslaved by Jon Irenicus and trapped in his dungeon circa 1369 DR.

Elvin Elminster (no relation) was co-owner alongside Dangus Barrowfold of Short and Tall Supplies, an equipment supply shop in Halfhap in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. He had no relation to the other Elminster.
Embril the Indentifier was a wizard inhabiting Suldolphor in the far eastern reaches of Calimshan in south Faerûn during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Elizabeth M. Soot was an author who dedicated their life to understanding evils of the world, and writing about how they could be overcome.
Most High Mornmaster Elurthron Belsurd was a high priest of Lathander inhabiting Suldolphor in the far eastern reaches of Calimshan in south Faerûn during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Elmerth Willowit was a half-elven thief assistant of Mortimer Mittlemer, an illusionist con-artist from Ravens Bluff, the Living City in the mid-14 century DR.

Elvauna Larethra was the matriarch of Milil who represented the Lord of Song throughout the late 14 and nearly all the 15 centuries DR. She served the Mililan faithful as high priestess of the Arbalest's House temple in Athkatla.
Elephon Stoneshoulder was a breeder of horses in the village of Maskyr's Eye in the Vast in the mid–14 century DR.
Elence Fielding was a merchant of the village of Imnesvale in the Umar Hills in the late 14 century DR.
Elvar the Grainlord was the ruler of Triel in the mid-14 century DR. He was impersonated a lot throughout the rest of the century.
Sir Elliot of Kness was a crusading paladin and criminal investigator who worked in Waterdeep and the Underdark in the 14 century DR.
Ellie was a young fisherwoman from the city of Elturel, whose life was cut short in the late 15 century DR.
Lady Elizabeth Lurian was a noble of House Lurian in the city of Procampur in the Vast in the late 14 century DR.
Fist Elthira Gossen was a member of the Flaming Fist who served the city of Baldur's Gate in late 15 century DR.
Elmarr Cardellith was a merchant lord in Sembia during the 14 century DR.
Elward Daunthideir, or Elward Varsoond Emmellero Daunthideir, was the steward of Lady Joysil Ambrur in Marsember in Cormyr during the late 14 century DR. He may have also been a slaver and smuggler.
Emblemat was a Netherese priest who served as the Chief Constable at Constabulary Branch Three in Eileanar before its destruction in .
Elranu Graywind was a renowned elven musical instrument crafter active sometime before the late 14 century DR.
Elgiva was a Netherese arcanist who worked at the Netheril Mint in Eileanar until its destruction in .
Elgrym Stormserpent was one of the heirs of House Stormserpent in the early-to-mid 15 century DR.
Elias Fischer was a commoner from the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Ellswin Glimrock was a master artisan refugee from the city of Elturel who found new home in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Elthaeris was a Chosen of Mystra, once the First among her Chosen.
Dread Brother Elryn was a Sharran priest during the mid–8 century DR.
Elliot was a member of The Guild and a bodyguard of its elected bursar in the late 15 century DR.
Emalline Brightbough was an officer of the Elves of Cormanthor in the late 14 century DR.
Eloise Thurman was an inhabitant of the Brampton neighborhood of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Embro Cymrych I was High King of the Moonshae Isles in the early 7 century DR.
Eluf the Steadfast was a dwarven member of Hal Stoutheart's Tethyamar expedition during the 1480s DR.
Elvere Sunberry was a reluctant client of the Sharran House of Grief and an inhabitant of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Elgar Buttercup Jansen was a brother of Jan Jansen, a gnome inventor, illusionist, and a turnip aficionado, who lived in Athkatla, Amn, during the mid–14 century DR.
Eleuthra Davos was a Ffolk druid from Moray in the Moonshae Isles in the late 15 century DR. She was killed in the late 1470s DR while battling drow beneath the island of Gwynneth.
Elynwyd was an elven clergy instructor of the Neverwinter Academy in Neverwinter in the late 14 century DR.
Eman was a dwarf warrior and member of the Three Coins Fellowship, an adventuring company active in the Delimbiyr Vale in the late 14 century DR, alongside Kars and Douver.
Laranlor Ellatharion was the ruler of Ardeep from the mid–6 to the early 7 century DR. He was one of the three kings of Phalorm until he vanished in battle.
Elistar "Watcher" Thistlebuck was a halfling thief inhabiting the city of Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR, and one of the original members of the Knights of the Sword Coast.
Errol was a human beggar from the City Core of Neverwinter in the late 14 century DR.
Evandriel was a moon elf Harper agent in Neverwinter in the late 15 century.
Lord Everran Summertree was a noble of Cormyr in the late 14 century DR.
Ambassador Ethur Anszim was the representative of the Red Wizards of Thay at their enclave within the city of Waterdeep.

Baron Estelner Ebonhawk was the head of Ebonhawk noble family of Cormyr in 1371 DR. He was young and unsure of himself, and widely thought to be a dunderhead trying to look good to the Crown. He led a troop of lancers, but had no skill with the weapon himself.
Baron Faneuil Hardisty was a warrior of Tethyr who attempted to bring an end to the anarchy within the region by any means available to him.
King Faerlthann was the first Obarskyr monarch and king of Cormyr.

Fairin Icemantle was a sage of the 6 and 7 centuries DR. Fairin was the author of the Treatise Against Blood-Metal, in which he expressed his reservations about orcslayer blades whose steel was poisonous to orcs. He feared that they would lead to the development of other alloys toxic to many races, and spread death and destruction. His treatise also discussed the dwarven attack on the orc kingdom of Vastar in the Year of the Spellfire, 610 DR, in which the dwarves wielded the new orcslayer blades. This provided the only first-hand account of the conflict to later generations. Fairin described the dwarven slaughter of the orcs, saying that they "run in waist-high riot across the land".

Lord Falzo Hawklin was a noble of the Hawklin family and a commander among Alusair Obarskyr's Blades. Lord Falzo Hawklin resided in a modestly sized manor on the northern side of Suzail's great Promenade with extensive gardens.
Faeryl Zauvirr was the Ched Nasadan ambassador to Menzoberranzan from ca. 1358 DR to 1372 DR.
Saint Fanal was a priest and saint of Ilmater and the founder of the Monastery of St. Fanal in the Alimir Mountains.
Falstaff was a doomguide who lived in the city of Neverwinter during the late 15 century DR.
Fandar was an elven swordsman in Elventree in Cormanthor in 1372 DR.
Falrinn Greatorm was a strange gnome smuggler in the late 15 century DR. He was acquianted with Kleef Kenric, topsword of the Marsember Watch.
Ezril Treewarder was a human druid of Eldath based in Elmwood in the Moonsea region in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Ezira Gloomdelve was a vampire and a top advisor to the mercenary lord Dalagor in Skullport in 1370 DR.
Fadela Bloodmane was a member of the House of Nasr of the High Desert of west Zakhara, and their likely successor, in 1367 DR.
Faersynd Floshin was one of the leaders of the daemonfey in the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR.
Faelindel was a young elf abjurer of Evermeet in the mid–14 century DR and a mage of Reilloch Domayr.
Faeryl Melarn was a senior drow priestess of House Melarn in Menzoberranzan.

Faerlaur Onthim was a senior member of the Sembian cell of the Cult of the Dragon during the late 14 century DR. As one of the Wearers of Purple, Faerlaur served on the leadership council that guided the Cult's operations in the region of Sembia, Cormanthyr, and the southern Dalelands.

Faerinaal () was an eladrin celestial paragon and consort of the eladrin queen Morwel. He dwelt in the Court of Stars with her and oversaw the defenses of that realm. He was also sworn to rescue eladrin captured by evil forces and taken to dangerous locations such as the Abyss. He lived with Morwel in the Gates of the Moon.
Faheed was a veteran adventurer who lived in Amkethran circa the .
Fanegonorom was a revenant that dwelled within ancestral crypts of the Korlasz family as of the mid–14 century DR.
Ezdush was a sage and a servant of Immurk living in the Pirate Isles during the mid–12 century DR.
Fadahl al-Araj, also called Fadahl the Crippled and previously Fadahl the Enlightened, served as vizier for the House of Tayif tribe in the High Desert of west Zakhara around 1367 DR.
Falias Emberthumb was a halfling merchant who sold mundane goods, cloth, and dresses from Waterdeep in the city of Daggerford circa 1372 DR.

Faldis was an accomplished and venerated elven warrior and member of Akh'Velahr who died before the advent of the Weeping War and was buried with honors in the depths of the Dwarven Dungeons of Myth Drannor.
Faizah Tin was a mage who lived in the Realms during the mid–14 century DR.
Facktoré was a rock gnome inventor and guard of Gnomengarde in the late 15 century DR.
Faerovel Hawntar was a priest of Auril in the late 15 century DR who originally hailed from the town of Glister.
Ezmerelda was the aunt of Rab Bitnez, the garlic-obsessed wizard from Liam's Hold, who authored the 101 Garlic Recipes cookbook.

Ezekial was a henchman, or perhaps pet, to the Talontar blightlord Damanda in . His form was contorted and twisted constantly, drapped in dull dark clothes. When hunting in Dun-Tharos, other demons often got to his prey before he did. While tracking Fallon and Araluen as his mistress bode him, he came across a strange swarm of demons that Fallon had disturbed, and was slain.

Fallon was a Nentyar hunter in . He betrayed the Nentyarch and kidnapped Araluen, intending to render her unto the Rotting Man; he eventually turned against his masters, but was slain in the process on Mirtul 7 of that same year.

Fadheela was the daughter of Mas'ud, a healer from Al Qahera in Raurin as of . She wore a blue caftan. Fadheela volunteered her father's guestroom for Thormud Horn after Kiril Duskmourn was allowed into the elven enclave. She also helped Kiril introduce herself to the village, and got her sharing the story of her trip, despite the traveler's surliness. She was taken aback when Prince Monolith appeared later during Kiril's sendoff, though she didn't get a chance to talk about it.
Faelfaril was the proprietor and innkeeper of Faelfaril's Inn in Bryn Shander in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Faerdaleeyn was a member of the Ala-min tribe within the Lake of Steam region during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Faerndel was a mage of Mourktar during the mid-3 century DR. He was offered the position of the Magister by Azuth, but turned it down, being the first recorded mage to refuse the position.
Faerdinalar the Enchanter was a famous mage sometime on or before the late 13 century DR. He was once the master of two different Magisters: Thornar Fleetmoor and Uldinus Lawkland.
Faereldan Chaserperi was the patriarch of the Chaserperi clan of mages as of the late mid-14 century DR.

Faerdar Ophardyn was a priest of the church of Oghma, called a Namer, based in the city of Selgaunt in Sembia in the late 15 century DR. By around 1480 DR, Faerdar had gained great prosperity from work in an arts or entertainment industry.
Faernor were specialty priests devoted to Berronar Truesilver, the Matron of Home and Hearth.
Falorian Windriver was the eldest son of Sabrast Windriver in the mid-14 century DR.
Falloor Malthind was a cobbler and retired warrior inhabiting Waterdeep, City of Splendors, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Fael, also known as Darcin Cole, was a cleric-merchant and, secretly, an agent of the Twisted Rune, from the village of Imnesvale in the Umar Hills of Amn in the late 14 century DR.

Fall-from-Grace was a succubus cleric and philosopher, who conquered her evil roots and after escaping the lower planes became the proprietress of the Brothel for Slaking Intellectual Lusts in the Clerks' Ward district of Sigil.
Fabbra was a Netherese arcanist who worked at Ioulaum Industries in Eileanar until its destruction in .
Falten was an employee of Baldur's Gate's Elfsong Tavern in the late 15 century DR.
Faldast was a warrior in the Frostfire Banner adventuring party in the mid–8 century DR.
Fador was a worker of the Lake of Steam region in the late 14 century DR.
Falael was a laborer, packer, and a delivery woman of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Falura was a halfling cook who worked under Chef Marjoram in Lady Jannath's Estate in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

King Faelrud was a king from the nation of Veldergauttland in the Whamite Isles. Faelrud represented Veldergauttland in a series of wild conflicts between various nations and pirates of the Whamite Isles at some point prior to the mass death of the population in the .
Faline Abbot was a knight of the Purple Dragons of Cormyr, who was stationed at Wheloon Prison in the late 15 century DR.
Ezkir Taromor was a Red Wizard of Thay that joined Droic Orgul's raid on Myth Drannor during the late 14 century DR.
Falcrow was the captain of the Sancarla during the late 15 century DR.
Faerdral was an assassin with the School of Stealth in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Faerim was a sailor from Waterdeep in the mid–14 century DR.
Fahid yn Nur al Suhal was a moneylender of Teshburl in Calimshan in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Fahd yn Sarsor al Nisr was a leader of the Rundeen mercantile organization, holding the position of a First Yrshelem, in the late 14 century DR.
Falchia was an azer blacksmith who dwelt and worked at a forge within a hidden library in the Calim Desert as of the late 16 century DR.
Faeniele Eshele was the representative of the wood elves of the High Forest to the Uthgardt of the Tree Ghost tribe at Ghostand in the late 14 century DR.
Faldorn was a power-hungry druid and the leader of the Shadow Druids that operated in west Faerûn during the mid–14 century DR.
Feringal Auck was the lord of Auckney in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Felix was chief lieutenant in the army of King Virdin Bloodfeathers of Damara when they fought the army of Zhengyi the Witch-King in the mid 14 century DR.
Fenmarel Mestarine () was the elven god of outcasts and isolationists. He was the teacher and protector of isolated elves and elf communities, and was known to use his avatar to patrol their borders.

Fender Stouthammer is a young dwarf of the Stouthammer clan. He was among those that followed Torgar when he left Mirabar for Mithral Hall. He was captured by Tos'un Armgo in a sneak attack with a poisoned blade. He managed to warn refugees from Nesmé of an ambush before being skewered by a sharpened branch. He is later healed by a Cleric of Lolth, Kaer'lic Suun Wett. Tos'un and Kaer'lic present him to Obould Many-Arrows as a gift. He returns home in the company of Drizzt Do'Urden.
Fayne was a fey'ri rogue who lived in Waterdeep and Westgate in the late 15 century DR. Her given name Ellyne came from the Elvish "elie en", which meant "Sorrow."
Feljack was an adventurer of the Vast in the mid–14th century DR
Feliane was an elf priestess of Eilistraee in Cormanthor and Velarswood in the mid–14 century DR.
Felitarr "Flyingfingers" Wendilar was a human man of the city of Tantras in the Vast around 1358 DR. He was a bard and an important member of the Harpers in the city.
Felodar Aumar was one of the Warring Princes of Athalantar and the most successful after his brother Belaur Aumar.
Farl was a thief and trader in Hastarl of the early and mid-3 century DR, and the best friend of prince Elminster Aumar.
Farnig Seasilver, nicknamed Farnig the Feckless, was the grand duke of Marsember in Cormyr in the late 15 century DR.
Favria was an assassin and the leader of an Ashmadai cult in Neverwinter in the late years of the 15 century DR.
Fangor Bloodclaw was a gnoll servant of Xivros, an emissary of the Red Wizards of Thay.

Feenoch the Five-Fingered was an infamous rogue and adventurer of the 1350s DR. In the Year of the Worm, 1356 DR, Feenoch was a member of a band of adventurers that rediscovered the fabled Barroch's Hold in the Glacier of the White Worm. However, they soon ran into a number of strange creatures, and were separated or killed. Feenoch, together with Yostur Ulhmond, made it to Orm to tell their story, though they would not be drawn on the matter of treasure. By the end of the year, it was said in Hillsfar they were trying to muster a larger group of adventurers, bearing sledges, perhaps intending to return.
Feldon Strongbeard was a dwarf who lived in the Protector's Enclave within Neverwinter in 1484 DR.
Fansa Windblossom was one of the four Cloakmasters of Eshpurta for the Shadow Thieves around 1370 DR.
Feluna Moonstar was a female human werecat cleric of Selûne in Waterdeep in 1372 DR.
Ferla Treerunner (also seen as Ferla Treeclimber) was a wild elf who lived in the Forest of Amtar in northern Dambrath.
Farim al-Kanafi was an inhabitant of Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.
